title: zone-shift-investigation-notes
content:
Context:
- Brief: intermittent "zone shift" where a subset of steady traffic originating in ap-southeast-1 suddenly got routed to eu-west-1 for ~8–12 minutes on 2026-03-09 03:14–03:26 UTC. Symptoms seen in app dashboards: spike in p95 latency, error rate stayed low but a few timeouts from client TLS sessions (client-observed session resets).

Timeline / quick notes:
- 03:12 UTC: minor autoscaler churn in ap-southeast pool (node replacement).
- 03:14 UTC: first trace of cross-region routing in routing-proxy logs (see sample log lines).
- 03:20 UTC: Canary route policy rollback applied (manual attempt) — did not fully revert for the affected prefix.
- 03:26 UTC: traffic returned to expected region after manual routing-table flush + restarting a single routing-proxy instance.

What I saw in routing-proxy logs (redacted IDs):
- 2026-03-09T03:14:08Z routing-proxy[proxy-7c9f] INFO route-eval request=req-6f3a4d route=ap-southeast-1 selected=eu-west-1 reason="fallback-policy:variant-unavailable"
- 2026-03-09T03:14:08Z routing-proxy[proxy-7c9f] WARN fallback-exec request=req-6f3a4d attempted-variants=[ap-southeast-1-gpu, ap-southeast-1-cpu]
- 2026-03-09T03:14:09Z kv-cache[cache-1] ERROR get-prefix ttl-mismatch key=prefix:usr:session:abc123 expected-ttl=3600 actual-ttl=120
- 2026-03-09T03:16:01Z route-engine INFO policy-sync job=sync-20260309 status=partial-update changed=3/12

Commands I ran while triaging (commands + quick outputs):
- kubectl -n routing get pods -o wide | grep proxy
  => proxy-7c9f (ap-sg-1) RESTARTS: 0 AGE: 3d
- kubectl -n routing logs proxy-7c9f --since=30m | head -n 100 | grep req-6f3a4d
  => saw the three lines above (route-eval / fallback-exec / kv-cache error)
- curl -sS https://ap-sg-1-routing.local/healthz -H 'Host: internal-routing'
  => 200 OK (but per-instance health was green)
- redis-cli -h redis-ap-sg -n 2 TTL prefix:usr:session:abc123
  => (integer) 120 (unexpected)
- redis-cli -h redis-eu -n 2 TTL prefix:usr:session:abc123
  => (integer) 3600
- jq '.policies[] | select(.prefix=="/v1/generate")' policies-config.json
  => shows policy version 2026-02-28 + canary flag true for ap-southeast-1 with fallback-order [eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1-cpu]  (hmm — order looks inverted)
- git log -n 5 --pretty=oneline routing-config-repo
  => PR 347 merged 2026-03-09 02:58 UTC (contains canary policy adjustments)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Policy propagation race: canary policy merged at ~02:58 UTC didn't fully reach all nodes; some proxies had an older fallback-order (eu-west-first) resulting in immediate fallback to eu-west for particular variant failures. Evidence: policy-sync partial-update + changed=3/12.
2) Redis TTL inconsistency across regions: local cache TTL for sessions in ap-sg was shorter (120s) vs eu (3600s). If routing decision logic depends on prefix recency/TTL, the shorter TTL could mark a session as "stale" causing fallback to alternative variants. Evidence: TTL mismatch command.
3) Node-level resource pressure during node replacement triggered transient variant-declaration failures (variant-unavailable) and fallback to the next policy entry. Evidence: autoscaler churn noted at 03:12 UTC.
4) Bad canary ordering: config authored with fallback-order inverted by mistake (eu-west preferred) for a small prefix. Evidence: policies-config.json check shows canary flag + inverted order.
5) BGP / cloud-level network flap unrelated to control-plane — less likely because we saw explicit fallback and TTL errors in app logs.

Immediate repro / experiments to run next:
- Re-run policy-sync in staging with instrumentation that logs full policy hashes on every proxy at sync time. Compare hashes across region proxies.
  Command idea: for pod in $(kubectl -n routing get pods -l app=proxy -o name); do kubectl -n routing exec $pod -- /bin/sh -c 'cat /etc/routing/policies/hash'; done
- Add a temporary check: on fallback, log the local policy file and the variant list that was attempted (to confirm inversion).
- Validate TTL write path: find code path that writes TTL for prefix session in ap-sg and instrument to log TTL value and source (who set it).
- Recreate small controlled test: issue 50 requests pinned to ap-sg variants while incrementally killing the ap-sg variant process to watch fallback ordering effects. Use test client with header X-Debug-Req to force logs.

WIP debugging notes / misc observations:
- Noticed a recurring log "kv-cache WARN delta-sync-slow" around the same time — maybe replication lag between redis clusters? Need to check replication lag (redis INFO replication).
- One of the proxies (proxy-3a2b) reported an earlier crashloop 6 hours prior and was recently replaced; its image tag was slightly older (release-2026-02-22) — possible that it had older route evaluation code.
- On-policy rollback attempt I did at 03:20 used the UI which triggers an async background sync; that may have left some proxies with stale in-memory copies until the next hot-reload. Manual restart fixed traffic.

Error snippets to search for in logs across clusters:
- "variant-unavailable"
- "ttl-mismatch"
- "policy-hash-mismatch"
- "preference-order-inverted"
- "delta-sync-slow"

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is routing decision using TTL as signal? (RQ to routing-engine owners)
- How does policy hot-reload guarantee full in-memory replacement (is it atomic?)
- Should we change canary rollout to a two-phase: config push + verified hash propagation before flipping canary flag?
- Is redis replication configured for synchronous ACKs for critical prefixes?

Immediate action items (me / Marcus / Priya):
- [Evelyn] Collect policy-hash from all routing-proxy pods in ap-sg and eu and attach to JIRA-5927 (by EOD).
- [Marcus] Check redis-replication lag metrics and set alert if >200ms for prefix DB (db 2) — follow up in #infra-region-fallback
- [Priya] Add quick logging patch on staging routing-proxy to dump fallback candidate list on fallback decision (PR target: routing-proxy/feature/debug-fallback-logs).

Notes-to-self:
- When reproducing, remember to use synthetic session IDs that avoid collisions with production TTLs.
- If manual restart fixes traffic quickly, it's OK as mitigation but we must find root cause (policy propagation / TTL issue).

Attachments / things to attach to ticket:
- policy-sync logs (03:10–03:30 UTC) from 6 proxies (ap-sg + eu).
- redis INFO replication at 03:15 UTC for ap-sg cluster and eu cluster.
- policies-config.json at HEAD and pre-merge PR-347 diff.
- proxy logs with req-6f3a4d (full trace).

Last thought: this felt like a configuration propagation/race more than pure network flapping — TTL mismatch is interesting but could be a symptom (old process setting TTL=120). Prioritize proving policy-hash divergence first.

End of scratchpad.
